subject: Request: EU failover RTO/RPO tighter than standard — contract addendum?
messages:
From: Shelley Tran <shelley@finserve.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: FinServe Legal <legal@finserve.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU failover RTO/RPO — request for tighter commitments

Hi Neha,

Following our internal readiness review, FinServe needs to tighten the EU failover targets in the upcoming contract. Our current requirement is:
- RTO (regional failover) <= 15 minutes
- RPO <= 5 minutes for user-facing inference traffic

We understand Redwood's standard multi-region SLA is 30 minute RTO and 15 minute RPO for warm-standby configurations. Given the regulatory profile of our payments flows in the EU, our compliance team is pushing for the 15/5 numbers.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support this as:
1) a paid addendum to the existing MSA (what uplift would you require?), or
2) a technical profile we can operate under a pilot to validate?

Attaching our high-level DR expectations and previous incident timelines. We're aiming to finalize SLA language with procurement/legal by 2027-03-10.

Appreciate a quick triage call tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,
Shelley
Director, Infrastructure
FinServe
Attachments: DR_Design_FinServe_v2.pdf
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Shelley Tran <shelley@finserve.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU failover RTO/RPO — request for tighter commitments

Shelley,

Thanks for the clear note and the attachment. I'm looping in Karthik (solutions) to confirm technical feasibility and Marcus (commercial) — copied in the next email — to size the uplift.

We can do a short call tomorrow at 10:00 CET to align on the key constraints and pilots; I put a calendar hold for 10:00–10:30 CET.

High-level: we recently shipped improvements to prefix/KV cache warmup and faster region warmup paths; for some customers we've improved effective RTO toward 15 minutes, but that often requires:
- dedicated warm-standby pool in region (capacity reserved)
- pre-warmed KV prefixes for active tenants or fast cold-start sequences
- stricter routing/fallback policies (no cross-region warm fallback allowed without explicit failback runbook)

I'll bring the configuration and a recommended addendum template to the call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-01T13:48:00Z
Subject: Re: EU failover RTO/RPO — technical feasibility notes

Neha / Marcus,

Quick tech assessment after reviewing Shelley's attachment and our internal runbooks:

1) Feasible path to 15/5 but only under a warm-standby + dedicated reserved capacity model:
   - Reserve N GPUs in eu-west-1 (or equivalent) as warm-standby. These nodes must maintain KV caches for critical tenants; continuous lightweight heartbeats keep caches hot.
   - Implement a prioritized prefix cache prefill for FinServe production prefixes (we'll need their typical traffic samples).
   - Reduce routing policy timeout thresholds to 10s for region health checks so failover initiation is faster.

2) Trade-offs:
   - Cost blowup is the main one — reserving dedicated warm instances increases baseline cost. The other is occasional brief increased error rates during failback if we don't do staged cache synchronization.
   - For RPO 5m, we'd recommend adding an optional short-term streaming replication pipeline for critical user state (small commits) — this depends on how much state FinServe stores per inference.

3) Pilot plan (recommended 8–12 weeks):
   - Week 0–2: config and sample traffic collection, runbook alignment
   - Week 3–6: spin warm-standby, prefill strategy validation, chaos testing (simulated region outage)
   - Week 7–10: production shadow failovers and SLA measurement, iterate

I'll prepare a short runbook draft and estimated resource profile (GPU types, memory, expected KV size). Attaching preliminary cost spreadsheet - see redwood-eu-warm-standby-costs.xlsx.

Happy to discuss on the call.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-02T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: EU failover RTO/RPO — commercial approach

Team,

Commercial recommendation for FinServe: offer a structured addendum with a three-phase engagement: pilot -> validation -> contracted SLA. Outline: 
- Pilot (90 days): Redwood will provision a dedicated warm-standby pool in EU; charge at cost+25% for reserved capacity and professional services (runbook + chaos testing).
- Post-pilot: if FinServe signs the addendum to guarantee dedicated capacity commitments, we move to a 12-month reserved capacity contract with an SLA amendment to RTO=15m / RPO=5m for EU region. Price uplift: estimated +18–22% on their current committed spend depending on exact GPU reservation.

Key commercial gating items:
- Signed Statement of Work and security attestation (we'll need SOC 2 scope confirmation)
- Agreed runbook and acceptance criteria (Karthik to author)
- DocuSign-ready SLA addendum and termination/rollback clauses (legal will draft)

I suggest proposing the pilot price and a DocuSign link for signatures in the 10:00 CET call follow-up. I'll own the pricing negotiation.

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Shelley Tran <shelley@finserve.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, FinServe Legal <legal@finserve.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: EU failover RTO/RPO — next steps and pilot offer

Hi Shelley,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion, here's the proposed path forward to validate and contract a 15-minute RTO / 5-minute RPO for EU failover: 

1) 90-day Pilot (finserve-DR-pilot):
   - Redwood provisions a dedicated warm-standby pool in eu-west-1 sized per Karthik's estimate (GPU profile attached).
   - Redwood implements prioritized KV prefill and short-term replication for critical keys.
   - We perform 2 scheduled controlled failover drills during the pilot and measure RTO/RPO against acceptance criteria.
   - Pilot pricing: reserved warm-standby at cost +25% + one-time PS fee for runbook and testing. Detailed numbers attached (redwood-eu-warm-standby-costs.xlsx).

2) Contract addendum after successful pilot:
   - 12-month reserved capacity agreement; SLA amendment providing RTO=15 min / RPO=5 min for EU region. Standard credits for SLA breaches apply but note there will be carveouts for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

3) Legal/commercial items:
   - We'll send an addendum in DocuSign for FinServe Legal review (link below). Please confirm who will sign on FinServe's side.

Action items for FinServe:
- Confirm acceptance of pilot scope and PS fee by 2027-03-07
- Share sample traffic/profile for KV prefill by 2027-03-10

DocuSign link (draft addendum): https://docusign.com/FS-2027-014/addendum
Jira runbook ticket: JIRA-RUNBOOK-4521

Attachments: DR_Design_FinServe_v2.pdf, redwood-eu-warm-standby-costs.xlsx

If that looks good I'll ask Legal to issue the pilot SOW and Marcus will get the pricing formalized.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
